passage_text: Researchers studied the pharmacokinetics of a novel anti-inflammatory drug, Compound X, in healthy volunteers. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover design, 12 participants received a single oral dose of 50 mg Compound X or placebo on separate occasions, with a washout period of 7 days. Blood samples were collected at baseline and at 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, and 240 minutes postdose. The plasma concentration of Compound X was quantified using a validated LC-MS/MS method. Table 1 summarizes the mean concentration (± SD) at each time point. The data indicate a rapid absorption phase, reaching a peak concentration (Cmax) at 30 minutes, followed by a gradual decline. The area under the concentration-time curve (AUC0–240) was ≈63,600 µM·min (trapezoidal rule). No adverse events were reported. These findings suggest that Compound X has favorable pharmacokinetic properties, with a short absorption window and a moderate elimination half-life, supporting its potential use as an acute anti-inflammatory agent.
stem: At which time point was the mean concentration of Compound X the highest?
explanation: Table 1 shows the highest mean concentration of 500 µM at 30 minutes.
trap: Students often assume the highest concentration occurs at the first postdose time point.

stem: Which of the following best describes the control condition used in the study?

options.A: Placebo given to the same participants on a separate occasion
options.D: A second 50 mg dose of Compound X

explanation: Correct: A) In the placebo-controlled crossover design each participant received Compound X and placebo on separate occasions, with a 7-day washout. Why the others are wrong: B) No other active drug was given. C) Only a 50 mg dose was used. D) The control condition was placebo, not repeated drug.
trap: Assuming the control received a lower or repeated dose of the same drug, when the passage describes a placebo condition.

stem: Calculate the average concentration of Compound X over the first 30 minutes (5–30 min) using the mean values.
explanation: Correct: A) (200 + 350 + 500)/3 = 350 µM. Why the others are wrong: B) 262.5 µM includes the 0 µM baseline in the average (4 values), but the question covers 5-30 min. C) 425 µM averages only the 15 and 30 min values. D) 450 µM averages only the 30 and 60 min values.
trap: Including the 0 µM baseline in the average (262.5 µM), which lowers the mean of the 5-30 minute values.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the data?

options.B: Plasma concentration fell below 10% of Cmax by 240 minutes.
options.C: Compound X reached Cmax at 30 minutes.

explanation: Correct: B) Cmax was 500 µM and the 240 min value was 100 µM, which is 20% of Cmax, not below 10%. Why the others are wrong: A) The concentration reached 200 µM (40% of Cmax) by 5 min. C) The 30 min value of 500 µM is the highest. D) The passage states no adverse events were reported.
trap: Misjudging 100 µM as under 10% of the 500 µM peak; it is 20%, so the statement overstates the decline.

stem: Which statement is best supported by the observed pharmacokinetic profile?

options.A: Rapid absorption supports an acute anti‑inflammatory effect.

explanation: Correct: A) Concentration rose quickly, reaching Cmax at 30 minutes, which fits a drug intended for acute use. Why the others are wrong: B) Absorption was fast, not slow. C) A high Cmax alone does not show toxicity; no adverse events were reported. D) The AUC of about 63,600 µM·min is not shown to be low, and AUC alone does not establish efficacy.
trap: Reading a high Cmax as evidence of toxicity rather than rapid onset.
